### `account add`

Add and authenticate an account (phone, bot token, or QR).

A bot token finishes in one call. A phone login starts here and finishes with `auth verify-code`, because somebody has to read a code and a daemon cannot prompt. `kind=bot` is recorded so that user-only commands fail fast.

```
tlgr account add [PHONE] [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · runs without an account · returns `AccountState`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHONE` | text | no | Omit with --bot or --qr. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alias` | text |  | Local name for the account. |
| `--api-hash` | text |  | api_hash for this account. |
| `--api-id` | int |  | api_id for this account. |
| `--bot` | flag |  | Log in as a bot with a token instead. |
| `--test-dc` | flag |  | Use the Telegram test DCs. |
| `--token` | text |  | The bot token. |
| `--qr` | flag |  | Use QR login instead of a phone code. |

Also invocable as: `tlgr login`

```console
$ tlgr account add +989123456789 --json
```

### `account check`

Health-check the stored authorization: authorized, revoked, banned or frozen.

Reports rather than raises, so one dead account cannot hide the health of the others. `frozen` carries Telegram's own appeal URL from `help.getAppConfig`; the appeal itself is a web form.

```
tlgr account check [ACCOUNT] [OPTIONS]
```

**paginated (`LOCAL` cursor) · runs without an account · returns `Page[AccountState]`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ACCOUNT` | text | no | One account; omit to check every one. |

Pagination is transport-level: `--limit/-n`, `--cursor TOKEN`, `--all` (walked inside the daemon, paced by the account's own rate limiter).

```console
$ tlgr account check --json
```

### `account logout`

Log out: revoke the authorization on the server and drop the session.

v1's `account remove` never called `auth.logOut`, so a removed account went on showing up in every other client's Devices list. The returned `future_auth_token` is a bearer secret: 0600 next to the session, capped at 20, dropped by `account remove`.

```
tlgr account logout [ACCOUNT] [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · destructive (needs `--yes` off a TTY) · runs without an account · returns `AccountState`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ACCOUNT` | text | no | Which account. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--keep-local` | flag |  | Keep the (now invalid) session file. |
| `--keep-token/--no-keep-token` | flag | `True` | Keep the future_auth_token for a code-less re-login. |

Also invocable as: `tlgr logout`

```console
$ tlgr account logout work --json
```

<details><summary>Catalog coverage (1 full, 3 partial)</summary>

Full: `auth.log-out`

Partial: `auth.clear-local-data`, `auth.future-auth-tokens`, `auth.logout-alternatives`

Wiping the alias is `account remove`; the token is minted by `auth send-code`; the support alternative is `account support get`.

</details>

### `account password get`

2-step verification status, and with the password the recovery address.

`--verify` is the shared SRP path every other sensitive operation reuses: call with `inputCheckPasswordEmpty`, and on PASSWORD_HASH_INVALID ask and retry. SRP_ID_INVALID refetches `account.getPassword`, because an srp_id is single-use.

```
tlgr account password get [OPTIONS]
```

**returns `PasswordState`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--password` | text |  | The 2FA cloud password (never in argv). |
| `--verify` | flag |  | Check the supplied password against the server. |

Also invocable as: `tlgr security password get`, `tlgr account password status`

```console
$ tlgr account password get --json
```

### `account website list`

Websites and bots you are logged into with Telegram Login.

```
tlgr account website list [OPTIONS]
```

### `account website revoke`

Disconnect one website, or all of them.

```
tlgr account website revoke [HASH]... [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · destructive (needs `--yes` off a TTY) · returns `WebSessionRevocation`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HASH` | text | any number | Websites to disconnect. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--block-bot` | flag |  | Also block the bot behind the login. |
| `--all` | flag |  | Disconnect every website. |

Also invocable as: `tlgr websites revoke`, `tlgr privacy website revoke`

```console
$ tlgr account website revoke 770 --json
```
